articles.title: Harry Kane ends England’s 25-year wait for a men’s Ballon d’Or
articles.summary: Striker has scored 91 goals for his country. Alexia Putellas picks up women’s award. Harry Kane is the Ballon d’Or winner for 2026, the first English man to win football’s most prestigious individual trophy in 25 years.
body: Two hours into a lavishly excitable ceremony at the Palladium Theatre in London, Kane’s name emerged from the final envelope to wild cheers inside the auditorium. The women’s Ballon d’Or, awarded moments earlier, was won by Alexia Putellas of London City Lionesses, a third Ballon, five years on from her first in the colours of Barcelona.

In the men’s voting, Kane finished ahead of co-favourites Lamine Yamal of Barcelona and Kylian Mbappé of Real Madrid, an outcome that will perhaps cause the familiar consternation among the hierarchy of those clubs, not to mention the vast online fan army attached to the superstar players in Kane’s wake.

But Kane is also a fully deserving winner of football’s ultimate gong. The L’Équipe-sponsored trophy is awarded by a vote of journalists and administrators across the footballing super-scape. For Kane, it is reward for a year during which he has won the European Golden Boot, played a major role in Bayern Munich’s Bundesliga title, captained England to a World Cup semi-final, and above all shown himself to be a wonderfully humble superstar player.

articles.title: Hearts chairman calls for greater transparency on key decisions
articles.summary: Reflecting on last season's final-day title disappointment, Hearts chairman Calum Paterson calls for "greater transparency and consistency around key decisions in Scottish football".
body: Talking to club media to mark his first year in the post, Paterson spoke with pride about coming so close to a first title in 66 years, but also voiced frustration around how last season's thrilling climax unfolded.
The Edinburgh side topped the Premiership table for 250 days but finished two points behind Celtic after a dramatic final-day defeat in Glasgow.

Lawrence Shankland struck first for the visitors, only for the reigning champions to find two late goals for a 3-1 victory, sparking a pitch invasion from jubilant home fans and a hasty exit for the beaten challengers, who expressed safety fears.

"The final week was difficult on a number of fronts," said Paterson. "Among other things we were disappointed by the unprecedented decision that as the team leading the league at the time of the split had to play our final game away from home.

articles.title: Kane ends England's 25-year Ballon d'Or wait - how he bucked the trend
articles.summary: Harry Kane becomes the first English player to win the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001 after being crowned the world's best player at a ceremony in London.
body: The 33-year-old Bayern Munich striker is the fifth Englishman to win in total, with Stanley Matthews (1956), Bobby Charlton (1966) and Kevin Keegan (1978 and 1979) the others.
Denis Law of Scotland (1964) and Northern Ireland's George Best (1968) are the other winners from the United Kingdom.
Real Madrid and France forward Kylian Mbappe finished second, while Barcelona and Spain attacker Lamine Yamal completed the top three.
"I am almost speechless. Being here in London has made it extra special," said an emotional Kane.

articles.title: Man Utd players set to return to training with Carrick's future still uncertain
articles.summary: Manchester United's players are set to return to training at Carrington on Tuesday - but it is still uncertain whether Michael Carrick will be in charge.
body: United head coach Carrick was at Carrington on Monday to watch the club's U21s take on Hull in a behind-closed-doors game.

The first-team players had a scheduled day off but Omar Berrada, the chief executive, and Jason Wilcox, director of football, also met at the training base, with their talks focused on next steps following Sunday's 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth.
It remains to be seen what the United hierarchy, which includes Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the part-owner, will decide.

United's defeat to Bournemouth saw Carrick drop captain Bruno Fernandes to the bench after he questioned his tactics following the 4-1 Champions League loss to Como. It extended United's winless run to eight games across all competitions.

articles.summary: Harry Kane has become the first English winner of the Ballon d'Or in 25 years after being honoured at a ceremony in London.
body: Michael Owen was the last player from England to receive the prestigious individual accolade in 2001, but Kane's incredible 73-goal haul last season for club and country earned him the award from French magazine France Football.
Bayern Munich forward Kane was a popular winner in the capital and has followed in the footsteps of Stanley Matthews, Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Owen as a Ballon d'Or winner from England.
Kane beat Real Madrid striker Kylian Mbappe and Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal to the award.

"Wow, I'm almost speechless," an emotional Kane said on stage. "First of all, thanks again to France Football and the Ballon d'Or for this amazing event. Being in London, it is extra special; it felt like a good omen.

articles.title: Putellas wins third Ballon d'Or - why her success is great for the WSL
articles.summary: London City Lionesses star Alexia Putellas claimed a record-equalling third women's Ballon d'Or.
body: The Spain international captained Barcelona to a quadruple last season, including Champions League glory, as she scored 26 goals and provided 15 assists for club and country.
The 32-year-old then sensationally joined London City Lionesses in one of the biggest transfers in WSL history.
Since her move in July, Putellas has scored three goals and has an assist in her seven WSL games.

The Women's Super League has never been able to boast a Ballon d'Or winner. Alexia Putellas' arrival has changed that; the latest recipient of football's most prestigious individual honour at Monday's ceremony in London, a town she surprisingly now calls home.
